messages:
sam: Quick experiment results from the Astra-12B bring-up. Ran fp16 / int8 / int4-hybrid across our 3 eval suites (conversational, summarization, extraction). posting the highlights.

maria: nice — paste numbers please, esp. cost deltas and any weird failure modes. :eyes:

sam: TL;DR: int8 looks like the best cost/quality sweet spot for GTN/chat features. int4-hybrid is tempting on cost but has brittle extraction failures.

sam: raw summary (median over 3 runs, 128 token prompt)
```
fp16       latency 180ms | cost $0.022/1k tokens | qual-score 0.912 (baseline)
int8       latency 125ms | cost $0.014/1k tokens | qual-score 0.892 (-2.2% rel)
int4-hyb   latency 100ms | cost $0.0098/1k tokens| qual-score 0.868 (-4.8% rel)
```

jon: are those eval-quality numbers average accuracy or a composite? what's the metric?

sam: composite utility score we use in eval harness: weighted(0.5 conv, 0.3 summary, 0.2 extraction). I can drop per-suite numbers.

sam: per-suite notes:
- conversation: int8 ~ -1.5% on turn-level coherence, int4 -3.3%
- summarization: int8 ~~ -1.8% rouge-L, int4 -4.5% (long context failures)
- extraction: int8 okay, int4 shows 8-12% drop on entity span exact-match (this is the scary one)

maria: extraction drop is concerning for GTN integrations (search result enrichment + entity tagging). Product will push back on >5% regressions.

eva: Product/GTN ask: can we mitigate without full fp16? e.g., selective fallback for extraction endpoints, or mixed-precision routing?

sam: yes — suggestions:
- default model: int8 for chat/summaries
- route extraction-heavy requests to fp16 or use a tiny verifier model for post-processing
- hybrid quant (int4) only for low-cost experimental tiers or assistant summaries where extraction isn't critical

jon: operationally how big is the unit-econ win? give delta per-1M tokens.

sam: unit econ (approx):
- fp16: $22 / 1M tokens
- int8: $14 / 1M tokens (~36% savings)
- int4-hyb: $9.8 / 1M tokens (~55% savings)

sam: so for GTN target throughput (50M tokens/mo) switching fp16->int8 saves ~ $400/mo per tenant at that volume. int4 saves ~ $610/mo but with risk.

maria: ok — product wants a recommendation for the GTN rollout doc. keep it crisp: one recommendation, one fallback, one monitoring KPI.

sam: propose this for GTN: 
1) Recommend int8 for all new chat endpoints by default. (Reason: ~36% cost reduction with <2.5% composite quality loss)
2) For endpoints that require extraction accuracy (>90% EM target), route to fp16 or use a verifier pipeline.
3) Canary rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 2 weeks with automated rollback on quality regression >2.5% composite or extraction EM drop >3%
4) KPIs to track in Console: composite score, extraction EM, latency p95, token cost per route.

eva: sounds good. add a short note for GTN marketing: "Per-user cost reduced by ~36% with parity UX for normal chat" — product will refine words.

jon: what about warm/cold cache behavior? any cold-start quality diffs?

sam: no quality diff due to cache. latency improves a bit on int8; cold-start throughput slightly better because kernels are faster.

ops-bot: flagged: create canary release job for astra-12b-int8 -> assigned to eng-oncall.

deploy-bot: canary started at 2001234598 :rocket: 5% traffic -> astra-12b-int8

maria: thanks — I'll draft the GTN guidance and include the rollout checklist. Sam, can you attach per-suite CSVs and the eval harness command you ran?

sam: uploading artifacts to S3 (link in thread): s3://redwood-evals/astra12b/2001234567/  — includes CSVs, scripts, and raw logs.

eva: one more ask for GTN doc: include a short verbiage on quality monitoring (human eval sampling plan + automatic alerts). I'll add that.

jon: +1 on int8 for general availability, keep int4 off by default.

sam: agreed. I'll open the PR with the recommended settings and the canary schedule.

maria: great work, team. will pair with product on messaging. :tada:
